case.title: Abubakar Musa and Another v. Dekina LGA and 6 Others

procedural_history.originating_proceedings: Motion on Notice dated 30th January 2014 and filed 4th February 2014 seeking leave to join additional defendants.
procedural_history.procedural_posture: Ruling on application for joinder of parties.
interlocutory_applications: Motion on Notice for joinder of Bassa Local Government Education Authority, Dekina Local Government Education Authority, Bassa District Education Committee and Dekina District Education Committee as defendants.
procedural_events: Written address in opposition filed on 7th February 2014.

material_facts: Claimants are teachers in the employment of Bassa and Dekina Local Government authorities.
Claimants complain about their sack or non-sack and non-payment of salaries and emoluments.
Bassa and Dekina Local Government Education Authorities are creations of statute.
Bassa and Dekina District Education Committees are advisory bodies to the Local Government Education Authorities on educational problems and adequacy of teaching staff.

chronology.event: Defendants filed written address in opposition.

admitted_facts: Defendants conceded that Bassa and Dekina Local Government Education Authorities are necessary parties.
Defendants opposed joinder of Bassa and Dekina District Education Committees.
disputed_facts: Whether Bassa and Dekina District Education Committees are necessary parties.
background_facts: Claimants are teachers in Bassa and Dekina Local Government areas.
The parties sought to be joined have statutory functions related to education.
facts.employment_relationship: Claimants are teachers employed by Bassa and Dekina Local Government authorities.
facts.contractual_relationship: Employment relationship between claimants and local government authorities.

causes_of_action: Employment dispute (sack and non-payment of salaries)

claims.claim: Leave to join Bassa Local Government Education Authority, Dekina Local Government Education Authority, Bassa District Education Committee and Dekina District Education Committee as defendants.
claims.legal_basis: Order 11(1) and (2) and 15 of National Industrial Court (NIC) Rules 2007 and inherent powers of the court.

reliefs_sought.relief: Leave to join Bassa Local Government Education Authority as defendant.
Leave to join Dekina Local Government Education Authority as defendant.
Leave to join Bassa District Education Committee as defendant.
Leave to join Dekina District Education Committee as defendant.

issues_for_determination.issue: Whether or not in the circumstances of this case, the presence of the parties sought to be joined is necessary for a just and effectual determination of this case.

questions_of_law: Principles governing joinder of parties under Nigerian law.

claimant_arguments: The presence of the parties sought to be joined is necessary for just determination.
The parties sought to be joined are creations of statute and necessary parties.
Joinder aims to effectually and completely adjudicate on issues and avoid multiplicity of actions.
defendant_arguments: Joinder is not automatic and must pass tests set by case law.
Conceded joinder of Bassa and Dekina Local Government Education Authorities.
Opposed joinder of Bassa and Dekina District Education Committees as their functions are not related to the claims.
submissions: Claimant submitted that joinder is necessary for just determination.
Defendant submitted that District Education Committees are not necessary parties.

party_authorities.authority: UBA Ltd v. Akparabong Community Bank Ltd & Another (2006) All FWLR (Pt. 320) 1129
party_authorities.proposition: Aim of joinder is to effectually adjudicate issues.

Peenok Inv. Ltd v. Hotel Presidential Ltd (1982) 12 SC 148

evidential_findings.evidence: Supporting affidavit paragraphs 2(c) and (d) deposing to functions of District Education Committees.

findings_of_fact.issue: Necessity of parties sought to be joined
findings_of_fact.finding: Bassa and Dekina Local Government Education Authorities and District Education Committees are necessary parties.

findings_of_law.finding: Joinder is governed by procedural rules and inherent powers; parties whose presence is necessary for effectual adjudication should be joined.

judicial_analysis.reasoning: The court considered the statutory functions of the parties sought to be joined and found that their presence would enable effectual settlement of all issues. The court applied principles from case law and the NIC Act 2006.

issue_analysis.issue: Whether the presence of the parties sought to be joined is necessary for a just and effectual determination of this case.

arguments.claimant: Parties are necessary for just determination; they are statutory bodies with relevant functions.
arguments.defendant: District Education Committees are not necessary parties as their functions are unrelated to the claims.

issue_analysis.judicial_analysis: The court examined the statutory roles of the parties and the principles of joinder. It found that the District Education Committees have advisory roles on educational problems and staff adequacy, which are relevant to the claimants' complaints about sack and salaries.
issue_analysis.holding: The parties sought to be joined are necessary, desirable, and proper parties.
issue_analysis.ratio_decidendi: A party whose presence is necessary for the court to effectually and completely adjudicate upon and settle all questions involved in a case should be joined.

holdings.holding: Parties sought to be joined are necessary parties.
holdings.result: Leave granted to join all four parties as co-defendants.

ratio_decidendi.principle: Parties whose presence is necessary for effectual and complete adjudication of all questions involved should be joined.
ratio_decidendi.application: The court found that the statutory functions of the parties sought to be joined are relevant to the claims, making them necessary parties.

legal_principles.principle: Joinder of parties is aimed at avoiding multiplicity of actions and settling all matters in dispute completely and finally.
legal_principles.source: Section 14 of NIC Act 2006; Awoniyi v. AMORC (2000) 10 NWLR (Pt. 676) 522.

statutory_interpretation.interpretation: The court has power to grant remedies to ensure all matters in dispute are completely and finally determined and multiplicity of proceedings avoided.
statutory_interpretation.application: Used to support joinder of parties.

precedent_analysis.proposition: Purpose of joinder is to enable court to effectively and completely adjudicate upon and settle all questions involved.

precedent_analysis.authority: Ibigbami v. Military Govt. Ekiti State
precedent_analysis.proposition: Joinder subject to conditions: right to relief arising out of same transaction and common questions of law and fact.
precedent_analysis.reasoning: Applied to find common questions of law and fact.
